entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_STORE_HASH
entries.description: The BigCommerce store's hash, the short ID in its API path (api.bigcommerce.com/stores/<hash>/). Not a secret. The connector checks that the token belongs to this store before reading anything.
howToGet: It is shown as the API path when the store-level API account is created (Settings > Store-level API accounts), between /stores/ and /v3/.
It also appears in the store's control panel address: store-<hash>.mybigcommerce.com.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN
entries.description: Access token of a store-level API account holding read-only scopes. BigCommerce can't report a token's scopes, so give it nothing but read-only scopes; the connector also sends only GET requests to its listed paths.
howToGet: In the BigCommerce control panel open Settings > Store-level API accounts > Create API account, type V2/V3 API token, named KaratOS.
Set these scopes to read-only and leave every other scope at None: Orders, Products (which covers price lists), Customers, Information & settings, Store inventory. Never choose modify.
Save, then copy the Access token straight into the host's secret store. BigCommerce shows it once; never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: BIGCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: Shared secret BigCommerce sends in the x-karatos-webhook-secret header of each webhook, set as a custom header when the webhook is created, since store webhooks carry no signature. Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
Create each webhook (POST /v3/hooks) with headers {"x-karatos-webhook-secret": <this value>}.
